items.title: 52193_Jay McShann oral history interview
items.q: the one who taught me in the third grade

ctx.x: I played the same two and three songs over all night, you know. I did know more than those two or three, you know, to myself, feel that I could do just but two or three songs, but I played, you know, I played that night and I think they gave me 80 cents and they gave me 80 cents. Well, I hadn't had no money in my pocket for so long, you know, it was just, oh, boy.

So anyway, they called us up to the board. This fella says, "Well, now, there's nothing we can do for you." He says, "There's no jobs coming through and everything's bad." He says, "You're going to have to write your folks for some money." Well, I knew there was no money at home, you know, and his folks didn't have no money. So he and I decided, I says, "Well, look, we got to leave here." And we felt so bad about it, we didn't go back to see the lady, Mrs. Grimes, you know, the one who taught me in the third…
So we caught a freight train and went to Knoxville.
